Well many big cities have really cool historic cemeteries with famous locals. You should really give one a visit!

  • Hollywood Forever Cemetery in California has many movie stars buried there.
  • Atlanta has Oakland Cemetery, a gorgeous garden cemetery.
  • I've now learned that Philly has Christ Church Burial Ground with founding fathers like Bejamin Franklin.
  • New Orleans has St. Louis Cemetery No. 1 which is an awesome windy cemetery where you can get lost in the endless mausolea!
  • Paris has the Père Lachaise Cemetery (Oscar Wilde, Jim Morrison) as well as the Catacombs!
  • Chattanooga National Cemetery is a huge veteran cemetery. Graves as far as the eye can see. (Also check out Forest Hills Cemetery while you're there)

And that is just the ones I can name off the top of my head. So many to choose from. Each and everyone has their own vibe, character, architecture, history, stories, and much much more. Frankly they're fascinating!

I'm not sure on your specific interests, but maybe go to a tour of a large cemetery in the closest major city?

The burial grounds are separate (but adjacent) to the church and have their own hours: http://www.christchurchphila.org/Visiting-Us/67/

The admission is $2 per adult and the hours are: Monday-Saturday - 10:00 AM - 4:00 PM Sunday - 12:00 PM - 4:00 PM

Also plan on hitting up the Visitors Center. The Constitution Center has the history, but the visitors center has a lot of near local flavor stuff if you talk to people: http://www.phlvisitorcenter.com/

EDIT: Before I forget - hit up the PA Masonic Lodge in philly: http://www.pagrandlodge.org/tour/onsite.html Totally unknown to the tourists, but they have stuff in there from both Ben Franklin, George Washington, a small museum, an awesome private library, and they let you touch most of the stuff like chairs from the early 1800s made of oak which simply doesn't exist anymore since all those forests were clearcut for ships.

EDIT EDIT: Valley Forge National Park's visitors center is free: http://www.nps.gov/vafo/planyourvisit/hours.htm It's a lot of hiking though but you can touch the cannons, etc. The Washington Chapel is also in your "graveyard" fetish and usually overlooked by the tourists: http://wmchapel.org/

Daniel Boone homestead is like $5 a head and worth going to: http://www.danielboonehomestead.org/

Hopewell Furnace: http://www.nps.gov/hofu/index.htm Again - not super touristy because PA does a shit job of advertising this stuff, but neat. Those all are a half hour to each other or so and 45 minutes from center city philly.
